title: Eager for Union
note: He and she both hurry towards union. She has made his intent to leave known, yet the eagerness rises in her from her own great longing, so this chapter follows the one on making signs known.

couplets.plain: To be drunk at a thought and elated at a glance: toddy can’t do this, but desire can.
couplets.pm: Elation at a mere thought and joy at a mere sight don’t come to those who drink toddy. They come to those who have desire. The first leaves the senses whole, and the second doesn’t. Toddy gives both only when it is drunk. With desire like this, how could I sulk?
couplets.context: Her friend teases her: he means to leave, so why don’t you sulk? She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: toddy can’t do this, but desire can
links.reason: Claims for desire alone a joy that comes at a thought and at a glance.
Toddy is the rival that fails the test, since it delights only when actually drunk.

couplets.plain: When desire comes full, as tall as a palmyra, you must not sulk even by a millet seed.
couplets.pm: When a woman’s desire grows beyond the size of a palmyra, she must not sulk with her lover even by a millet seed. If she sulks, her suffering grows. She seems to be giving others good advice, but she is telling of her own eagerness.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: A palmyra’s height of desire leaves no space for a millet seed’s worth of sulk.

couplets.plain: Though he shows me no regard and does just as he likes, my eyes can’t rest without seeing my husband.
couplets.pm: Though he slights me and does only what he wants, my eyes won’t be content without seeing my husband. She lays her own eagerness on her eyes. Being like this, how could I sulk?
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she
couplets.sensitive: presents needing one who neglects her as natural

links.quote: my eyes can’t rest without seeing my husband

couplets.plain: I went there to sulk, my friend, but my heart forgot that and went to join him.
couplets.pm: Friend, before I saw him I thought over his fault and set out to sulk with him. Once I saw him my heart forgot that and went to union. What use was my going? My heart betrayed me at that moment, so the sulk was never finished.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: I went there to sulk, my friend
links.reason: Owns up to her friend that the plan to sulk fell apart.

couplets.plain: Like the eye that can’t see the stick painting it with kohl, I can’t see my husband’s faults when I see him.
couplets.pm: The eye sees the kohl stick at other times, but while it is being painted it can’t see the stick’s blackness. So too I see my husband’s fault wherever he isn’t, and when I see him I can’t see it. This is my nature, so sulking won’t succeed in future either.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: When I see him I see no faults. When I don’t see him I see nothing but faults.
couplets.pm: When I see my husband, I don’t see his faults. When I don’t see him, I see nothing else. The faults I told you about before aren’t in sight now, so I didn’t sulk.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Like people who jump into a flood knowing it will sweep them away, what use is it to sulk, knowing it will fail?
couplets.pm: Like those who leap into a running flood knowing it will carry them off, what do I gain by sulking with my husband, knowing the sulk won’t hold to its end? If the text reads “I knew it fails”, then: like those who leap in to learn how the water carries, I once sulked to learn its end, found it fails, and shouldn’t do it again.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Your chest, you thief, is like toddy to those drunk on it. However shameful the harm it does, they want more.
couplets.pm: You deceiver, your chest is to us like toddy, which does shameful harm to those who drink it and is craved all the more. That harm is the loss of modesty, reserve, good conduct and good sense. Your chest does this to us, and we want it more and more. That is why she calls him a deceiver.
couplets.context: Her friend sees her eagerness for union, and says this to him.
couplets.speaker: maid
couplets.sensitive: welcomes back one who hurts and shames her

links.quote: is like toddy to those drunk on it
links.reason: She is the drinker who keeps going back to the toddy that disgraces her.

couplets.plain: Desire is softer than a flower. Few ever find it at its peak.
couplets.pm: The joy of desire is softer than a flower, which loses its fresh scent at a touch. Few in this world know that and reach its peak. Two people must match in intent, longing, enjoyment and joy at one time, with the right place, time and means. If any of these differs a little, it wilts. Our intent doesn’t match, so I don’t have it. He says this to end her sulk.
couplets.context: She is sulking and won’t be won over by his pleading, and he says this.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Few ever find it at its peak
links.reason: Says what desire is: so soft that few ever find it at its peak.

links.quote: Desire is softer than a flower.
links.reason: The flower sets the measure of softness, and desire goes beyond it.

couplets.plain: She sulked with her eyes alone, then gave way, more eager to embrace than I was.
couplets.pm: Once, when I went eagerly to embrace her, she sulked with her eyes alone, with no word, her eyes only reddening. Then, more eager for the embrace than I was, she forgot even that and joined me. I am the same man now, so this woman who stands sulking with no eagerness is not she. That woman wouldn’t keep up a sulk for long.
couplets.context: She is still sulking, and he goes on.
couplets.speaker: he
